hero.title: IES, QuickBooks, or a legacy ERP?
hero.subtitle: Every option has trade-offs. Here is where each one shines and where it falls short for a growing finance team.
intro.title: Trade-offs, not just talking points
intro.body: Pick a tab to see the full picture for each option, upsides and downsides side by side.
item-1.title: Intuit Enterprise Suite
item-1.tagline: AI-native ERP built for multi-entity finance teams
item-1.pros: Consolidates hundreds of entities in one view
AI agents automate the month-end close
Go live in as few as 14 days
item-1.cons: More capability than a single entity needs
New platform to learn versus staying put
item-2.title: QuickBooks Desktop
item-2.tagline: Familiar accounting for a single company file
item-3.title: Traditional ERP
bestfor.title: So which is best for whom?
best-1.title: Intuit Enterprise Suite
best-1.body: Growing businesses with multiple entities that have outgrown basic accounting but do not want legacy ERP overhead.
best-2.title: QuickBooks Desktop
best-2.body: Single-entity businesses with straightforward books and no near-term consolidation needs.
best-3.title: Traditional ERP
best-3.body: Very large enterprises with dedicated IT and highly specialized configuration requirements.
bottomline.title: Our recommendation
bottomline.body: For most growing, multi-entity finance teams, Intuit Enterprise Suite hits the sweet spot: ERP-grade consolidation and AI automation without the cost, complexity, or disruption of a traditional ERP rollout.
